newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia has flat net grain balance - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Russia has flat net grain balance - newspaper.

text.p: Russia now exports as much grain as it imports, the government daily Rossiiskiye Vesti said on Friday, putting total grain imports last year at four to five million tonnes.
It also put carryover stocks from last year's harvest at a high 10 million tonnes, saying supplies had accumulated as the livestock sector contracted further.
Winter wheat yields from the 1997 crop were forecast to rise to an average two tonnes per hectare from 1.79 last year.
Spring wheat yields would rise to 1.3 tonnes from 1.1 tonnes, maize to 2.6 tonnes from 1.75, winter rye to 1.5 tonnes from 1.43 and spring barley to 1.6 from 1.29.
The newspaper said it had received the figures from Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun.
Russia's net grain output this year is officially forecast at 70 million tonnes, little changed from 1996's 69.3 million tonnes, the second poor showing in a row.
But some analysts and officials say output may rise to 75-80 million net tonnes.
